a8cfe0e7c3.q: How do PE-backed aggregators structure deal payments to justify premium acquisition prices while managing risk?
a8cfe0e7c3.a: PE-backed aggregators typically put 40-50% cash down at closing, with the balance split equally between rolled equity in the acquirer's firm and earn-out or performance-based payments. Sellers must achieve 10-20% growth over four to five years to receive full value, which essentially requires retaining all clients and acquiring new ones. If growth targets are not met, sellers may receive only the initial cash payment while the equity portion remains illiquid for many years.

4ad57f236b.q: What are the three key variables in retention clauses and clawback provisions used in acquisition deals?
4ad57f236b.a: The three key variables in retention clauses are: what you measure (revenue, AUM, or clients), when you measure (typically 12 months after closing, occasionally 18 months), and what your target is (usually 90% if paying normal value, or 95-100% if paying a premium). The measurement metric directly ties to price, with revenue being the most common historically, though client count measurement is increasing in popularity because it eliminates market risk.
